claims.text: ADR 0017 keeps one Flutter code base for every platform; stage-4 adds no android/ or ios/ folder, so the app is built only for the browser; the same code can be built for Android and iOS when enough shops need an installed app.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0017-giu-mot-ma-flutter-cho-moi-nen-tang.md @ stage-4, sections Bối cảnh, Quyết định, Ý kiến đã nhận

claims.text: Push needs a phone build that ADR 0017 has not made, so CT-5 uses email: a reply unread after 5 minutes (assumed) goes through the outbox and Notifications, a separate service with its own database, emails the customer under ADR 0027.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/support-chat-requirements.md @ stage-4 (CT-5 and note below the scenarios); ADR 0032 @ stage-4 lines 46-47

claims.text: ADR 0032 revisit conditions: the app gets a phone build (push replaces email for CT-5); ASP.NET Core gets an official SignalR client for Dart; connections per Pod exceed the measured headroom. CT-5: a shop replies while the customer has no chat screen open; the customer gets email.
The review's 'ADRs to write' section: ADR 0032 (exists); push for a phone build: a new ADR when that build exists.
Each chat message is saved with its conversation, shop and sender; the shop comes from the access token (from release 2), and row-level security applies as in ADR 0013.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0032 @ stage-4 lines 39-41, 48; support-chat-design-review.md @ stage-4 line 103

claims.text: ADR 0013: a request's shop comes from the verified access token, not from a parameter the client sends; code filters every query by shop_id, and row-level security is the second guard for a query that forgets the filter.

Ranked drivers of the chat design: 1 message reaches an open screen within seconds; 2 no message lost when delivery fails; 3 staff never see another shop's chats; 4 chat never takes capacity ordering needs.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/support-chat-design-review.md @ stage-4 lines 15-24; docs/team/support-chat-requirements.md @ stage-4, Driver xếp hạng

claims.text: The sale-day question is recorded as a risk: a cap on connections per shop in the style of ADR 0016, set after measuring; next step 'measure connections per shop'; owner the Ordering team. The same risk is in the review's risks table.
Chat is not built at stage-4: no service, endpoint or chat code exists in the repository; connection figures (about 200 at peak, about 100 per Pod with 2 Pods) are assumptions.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0032 @ stage-4 lines 7-8; support-chat-design-review.md @ stage-4, Ước lượng và giả định

claims.text: The module question is answered by ADR 0032 driver 4: connections held for a long time would share Pods, limits and canary releases with order-taking; ADR 0032's comments section records the same question from a backend developer, decision unchanged.
claims.source_hint: support-chat-design-review.md @ stage-4 line 106; ADR 0032 @ stage-4 lines 67-71

claims.text: The review ends with sections: risks and open questions, ADRs to write, challenges. Challenge table: five rows; four next step 'none', no owner; sale-day row 'measure connections per shop', Ordering team; release row cites ADR 0019 (release strategy per component) and 0032.
ADR 0032 chooses a separate service, DonHang.Support; its consequences: one more service, one more database, one more HTTPRoute. The module option adds no service.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0032 @ stage-4 title, Các phương án, line 35, line 56; docs/adr/0019-chien-luoc-phat-hanh-theo-thanh-phan.md title

claims.text: A module for chat is the better choice when no driver protects ordering from chat, or when chat connections are too few to matter next to ordering's limits; with driver 4 ranked and about 200 long-held connections (assumed), a separate service wins.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0032 @ stage-4, Các phương án and Ý kiến đã nhận; design.l4.trade-off-points

claims.text: ADR 0016 caps a shop at a fixed share of a shared limit; the cap is not a reserved share, so what a shop leaves unused stays open to others.

Risks table: how the connection carries the access token when the WebSocket opens is open, owned by the Ordering team, decided when building; whether the Gateway closes a long silent connection is open, owned by the platform team, checked before building.

Filtering rows only in the staff screen still sends other shops' rows to the client; taking the shop from the access token where rows are read, with row-level security as a second guard, keeps them from leaving.
If chat were a module of DonHang.Api, an API release would close chat connections and chat connections would compete for the Pods that take orders.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0032 @ stage-4, Các phương án, Hệ quả (each release closes connections of replaced Pods)

claims.text: The recorded sale-day risk names only a cap per shop; ADR 0032's third revisit condition, connections per Pod exceeding the measured headroom, is a separate check.

beyond_scope: Fifth challenge row (release of Support) read from the quoted table; reuses the previous lesson's trade-off, not re-taught.
What-if on the shop id as a WebSocket parameter reads an open row of the review's risks table; no connection cap is designed (depth_notes).
